speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your painful ulcerative lesion, can you tell me how long the sore has been present and if you have a history of diabetes or poor circulation?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Can you describe the current appearance of the ulcer, specifically the color of the base, the condition of the edges, and whether there is significant swelling or redness spreading from the site? Also, have you noticed any fever, joint pain, or changes in your eyes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of a painful ulcer with purplish irregular borders, a history of an insect bite, and your previous episode of uveitis strongly suggests Pyoderma Gangrenosum, especially given your Crohn's disease history. To rule out other causes like infection or vasculitis, I will order some tests and request images of the lesion.

REQUEST TEST: Wound Culture
REQUEST TEST: ANA
REQUEST TEST: ESR
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the test results; the normal readings help rule out certain infectious and autoimmune causes. Given the history of Crohn's disease, the characteristic appearance of the ulcer with purplish borders, and the phenomenon of pathergy following the ant bite, the clinical picture is highly consistent with Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
